631144265.accepts_evidence: Only organizations given an invitation code may submit a proposal, and the foundation says it cannot respond to unsolicited inquiries; it sometimes identifies opportunities through bank associates. https://www.regions.com/about-regions/community-engagement/regions-foundation
631144265.contact: No foundation phone or email published
631144265.deadlines: No deadlines given; the board reviews applications quarterly.
631144265.eligibility: Organizations with a current IRS tax-exempt designation that permits charitable contributions, able to show quantifiable impact measures, and holding an invitation code.
631144265.geographic_limits: Programs must be delivered inside the Regions Bank footprint, described as 16 states across the Southeast, Midwest and Texas (states not listed on the page).
631144265.how_to_apply: By invitation only: an invited organization enters its application through the foundation's online system using the invitation code, with standard documents (IRS letter, W-9, two years of audits, budgets, board list, evaluation plan). Separate from this, Regions Bank takes contribution and sponsorship proposals from community partners through its own community engagement portal.
631144265.name: Regions Foundation
631144265.not_funded: Individuals, sponsorships, fundraising events, meals, programs outside the Regions footprint, and programs outside the three priorities.
631144265.notes: Two doors: the Foundation (invitation code required) and Regions Bank's corporate contributions and sponsorships, which the bank's community engagement portal accepts proposals for (bank program details not read). The practical route to a foundation invitation is a local Regions banker or community affairs associate. Kansas is not obviously in the footprint; check the bank's branch map before pursuing for a Kansas client.
priorities: economic and community development (affordable housing, small business development, neighborhood revitalization, job creation)
education and workforce readiness (college and career readiness, credentials and employment, educational access, educator training)
financial wellness (financial education, planning resources, homebuyer readiness)
